doc.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The state of jazz, future plans and close
title: China and Hong Kong
summary: He has never been to China and recalls Hong Kong on a Philip Morris tour.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: No, I haven’t. That’s one place I haven’t been. I don’t even know if they – yeah, because I’ve talked to people who have been there.
It’s opening up more and more, Shanghai, Beijing.
I would love to go, but I’ve never been. Only in the airport. Well, not in Beijing. I have been to Hong Kong
That’s night and day compared to the mainland. Hong Kong is beautiful, though. I love Hong Kong. How about you? You had a good time when you were there?
Did you play at the Cultural Center, that hall? Because that’s beautiful.
I don’t remember. This was with the Philip Morris tour. So this was 15, 20 years ago.
Maybe the hall wasn’t even around then.

But it was great. There was actually a jazz club there that we went to, to hang out. It was called – I think it was called the Jazz Cafe or something like that. There was a group from Japan working there. No, I would love to go to China. I did get a call one time. or an e-mail, from somebody a few years ago about the Beijing Jazz Festival. But I was working at the time, so I couldn’t. I sent an e-mail to the effect that unfortunately I’m working, but some other time I would love to do it. But I never heard back any more. I’ll have my manager look into it.
